workload.name: Demonstration arithmetic block
workload.description: A small Clifford+T circuit with Toffoli gates, used to demonstrate the KetQat Intelligence pipeline end to end. It is not a real workload and its numbers are not an estimate for one.

problem_size.description: Demonstration instance; no real problem size is claimed.

notes: Demonstration fixture. Not evidence about any workload, device, organisation, or advantage claim.
Static count over the circuit as written. No synthesis, decomposition, or optimization is applied.
Duration not estimated: the hardware snapshot does not characterize every gate used.
Success probability not estimated: the hardware snapshot does not characterize every gate used.
No hardware snapshot supplied, so duration and fidelity are not estimated.

classical_baseline.compute_environment: Illustrative single-core statevector simulation of the same six-qubit circuit.
classical_baseline.workload_size: Six qubits, twenty-two gates. Demonstration instance.
classical_baseline.evidence_note: Illustrative figure for the demonstration, not a measurement of any classical system. Supplied so the runtime comparison and its refusals can both be exercised.
limitations: Not a measurement. Every comparison derived from it demonstrates the calculation, not a result.
Classical simulation of a six-qubit circuit is trivial. This baseline is not evidence about any workload where quantum computation would be considered.

scenarios.name: Conservative
scenarios.rationale: Device parameters at the pessimistic end of what good superconducting hardware has demonstrated. Chosen so that a favourable answer here is not an artefact of favourable assumptions.

hardware.name: Generic reference device, conservative parameters
hardware.source: A conventional pessimistic reading of demonstrated two-qubit error rates on superconducting devices, with the 1 microsecond surface-code cycle used throughout the fault-tolerance literature.
limitations: Not an observation of any specific device; a convention chosen to bound the optimistic case.
No capacity is asserted, so capacity-dependent thresholds are refused rather than guessed.

qec.source: Rotated surface code under circuit-level depolarizing noise; threshold ~1% and p_L = 0.03 (p/p_th)^((d+1)/2) after Fowler et al. (2012), arXiv:1208.0928.
limitations: The prefactor is fitted, not derived; the alternative published value 0.1 is reported as model sensitivity.
Leading-order logical error only; no decoder-specific correction is applied.
One QEC scheme is modelled in this version. Other codes are not costed.

decomposition.source: Standard Clifford+T decomposition: one Toffoli costs 4 T gates.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.rationale: The parameters most fault-tolerance resource analyses use: a 1e-3 physical error rate and a 1 microsecond surface-code cycle. Comparable with published estimates that state the same assumptions.

hardware.name: Generic reference device, standard literature parameters
hardware.source: The physical error rate and cycle time used as the standard case in surface-code resource analyses, for example Gidney and Ekera (2019), arXiv:1905.09749.
limitations: A convention, not a device. Two machines meeting this error rate can differ in every other respect.
No capacity is asserted, so capacity-dependent thresholds are refused rather than guessed.

scenarios.name: Optimistic
scenarios.rationale: Device parameters an order of magnitude better than the standard case, and a five-times faster cycle. This is a target, not an observation: it states what hardware would have to reach, which is the question the threshold engine answers rather than a prediction that it will.

exact_arithmetic: Magic states: 8 T + 4 x 3 Toffoli = 20.
Logical cycles: max(depth 9, 1) = 9.
Occupied logical patches under LATTICE_SURGERY_2D: 20 (algorithm register 6).
Per-patch footprint: 2 x 9^2 = 162 physical qubits.
Cycle-limited runtime: 9 cycles x 9 rounds x 1000 ns = 8.100e-5 s.
Distillation: 2 level(s) of 15-to-1, 225 raw states per output, 4500 raw states total.
model_assumptions: SURFACE_CODE_ROTATED under circuit-level depolarizing noise.
Logical error model p_L = 0.03 (p/0.01)^((d+1)/2), fitted rather than derived.
2 d^2 physical qubits per logical patch.
One logical cycle occupies `distance` surface-code rounds.

The error budget is allocated across the algorithm's own logical qubits. Routing patches are charged for space but not against the budget, which understates the required distance for routing-heavy layouts.
Factory footprint model: 15 logical patches per distillation level at the factory distance. A reading of the standard construction, not a measured or published figure.
Factory throughput model: one distilled state per 10 surface-code rounds per factory, with 1 factory(ies) in parallel. A model, not a measurement.
Only the leading order of the 15-to-1 error polynomial is used.
warnings: The magic-state factory is 60% of the machine -- larger than the algorithm it feeds. A T count reported without this footprint understates the hardware requirement here by more than a factor of two.
This is a demonstration fixture. It is not evidence about any real workload, device, or organisation.

exact_arithmetic: Magic states: 8 T + 4 x 3 Toffoli = 20.
Logical cycles: max(depth 9, 1) = 9.
Occupied logical patches under LATTICE_SURGERY_2D: 20 (algorithm register 6).
Distillation: 0 level(s) of 15-to-1, 1 raw states per output, null raw states total.
model_assumptions: SURFACE_CODE_ROTATED under circuit-level depolarizing noise.
Logical error model p_L = 0.03 (p/0.01)^((d+1)/2), fitted rather than derived.
2 d^2 physical qubits per logical patch.
One logical cycle occupies `distance` surface-code rounds.

The error budget is allocated across the algorithm's own logical qubits. Routing patches are charged for space but not against the budget, which understates the required distance for routing-heavy layouts.
Factory footprint model: 15 logical patches per distillation level at the factory distance. A reading of the standard construction, not a measured or published figure.
Factory throughput model: one distilled state per 10 surface-code rounds per factory, with 1 factory(ies) in parallel. A model, not a measurement.
Only the leading order of the 15-to-1 error polynomial is used.
warnings: This is a demonstration fixture. It is not evidence about any real workload, device, or organisation.

Logical counts are DERIVED; hardware parameters are USER_ASSUMPTION at MEDIUM confidence; the classical baseline is USER_PROVIDED; the quantum cost model is absent. These are different kinds of claim and are not averaged into a score.
The widest spread comes from the physical error rate: a 40.1x range in total physical qubits across the swept values.

assessments.explanation: Under this model the computation needs 8,100 physical qubits and 0.000200 s at code distance 9. The computation is technically feasible under this model, but no economic conclusion can be made because no quantum machine-cost assumption was supplied. The binding constraint is magic-state throughput, not logical-qubit capacity: the runtime is set by how fast distilled states arrive rather than by the depth of the logical circuit. A surface-code cycle below 250 ns would be required to beat the supplied classical runtime. This assessment is built from a demonstration fixture and is not evidence about any real workload or device.
